english_research_meaning: The original explicitly separated first-run configuration/directory preparation from a repeated launch that reads saved bootstrap state and starts without repeated questions.
defeater_or_limit: An installer or externally managed platform can implement this user outcome differently; a first-run splash is not a supported requirement or installation test.

english_research_meaning: The old per-user Git-updating launcher required an offline fallback that logs failure and continues from the last local revision rather than refusing to open.
defeater_or_limit: Fallback must be qualified as unverified historical behavior: a prior checkout may contain unsafe/unsupported code or dependencies, so a managed release needs integrity and compatibility policy.

english_research_meaning: The roadmap distinguished virtual-environment dependency refresh from launching the separately loaded GUI with effective profile, paths and environment context, including restart when GUI code changed.
defeater_or_limit: A live branch update and local venv rebuild are not a package-level atomic upgrade or proof of matched API versions; the modern AppDock activation and installed package graph govern current behavior.

english_research_meaning: The dated UI plan proposed declaring task names, parameters, handlers, source links and output directories as loadable config instead of hardcoding every task in GUI, while all tasks reused domain-core execution.
defeater_or_limit: Configuration-driven task discovery is a research proposal, not evidence of installed dynamic providers or a permissioned arbitrary-Python dispatcher; the pinned Windows catalog is explicitly hand-curated.

english_research_meaning: The roadmap paired product/tray icon resources with distinct bootstrap/update/environment/task logs, human-readable failures and degraded startup after network, repository, mapped-drive or dependency problems.
defeater_or_limit: Visible degraded launch is not evidence that domain work can run or that cached data is authentic; log completeness, exact version and resource readiness need separate checks.
